finding: Same task template in train and test inflates scores
evidence: 0 templates in two folds, 0 shared dev / test (after the split)
decision: Split grouped by template; fixed test set of the original task-disjoint split

finding: The simulated world gives away the category
evidence: world purity 91%–99% by domain (email: 32%); world lookup F1 0.838
decision: Anonymise world identities (relational placeholders) before any feature

finding: Worlds cannot be grouped together with templates
evidence: 1060 of 1136 dev worlds in two folds or more
decision: Text-only world probe as the control; world-grouped folds as a robustness check

finding: Anonymisation removes the world signal from the text
decision: Models read the anonymised tables only (`read_*(anonymized=True)`)
Report the position-only baseline as the floor; step index and history length never features

evidence: trajectory length alone ROC-AUC 0.58 for y_traj

finding: Injections are readable for full attacks, often not for partial / delayed ones
evidence: any indicator visible: full 100%, partial 65%, delayed 46%
decision: Mask generator artefacts (generic upper-case label rule, policy codes, amounts); recall by attack type and by visibility

finding: The generated thought confesses the attack
evidence: confession words in thought: 75% of H partial
decision: Variant without `thought` is the reference; with `thought` reported as an ablation rung

finding: Imbalanced targets; the step to stop is the first hijacked one
evidence: y_scan 9.9%, y_gate 17.4% of steps; 5536 first H (7.8% of steps)
decision: PR-AUC as the main metric; class weights; business metrics at the first alert

finding: The scanner can only anticipate on delayed attacks
evidence: injection → hijack gap ≥ 2 steps only for delayed attacks (93% at exactly 2)
decision: Detection lead reported on delayed attacks only

finding: The fixed test set is small
evidence: 35 templates; expected 95% interval width on it: PR-AUC ±0.071, recall at 1% FPR ±0.068 (reference score, gate)
decision: Report every test result with a template-cluster bootstrap interval; model choice on the 5 dev folds

evidence: design effect 7.4 (median over gate metrics): a step-level bootstrap would understate the interval
decision: Resample templates, never steps; paired bootstrap for model comparisons

finding: Very low FPR targets are hardly measurable
evidence: expected false positives at 0.2% FPR: 16 on the test set, 27 on an inner validation part
decision: Keep 0.2% as a secondary operating point, reported with its observed FPR

finding: Domains differ in prevalence and attack mix
decision: Leave-one-domain-out, with the threshold transferred from the training domains
